resources.name: Box2D v3 (box2d3-wasm)
resources.role: 2D rigid-body physics as WASM in Node, stepped at a fixed timestep and baked to per-frame positions
resources.summary: Box2D v3 is Erin Catto's C engine; box2d3-wasm is a third-party npm build of v3.2 with compat (no threads) and deluxe (SIMD and threads) variants. The C-style API steps a world by a fixed dt, so positions are read per frame and cached. The author states cross-platform determinism; the fixture checks only single-machine repeatability.
use_when: 2D rigid bodies (circles, boxes, joints) baked to per-frame transforms in Node and replayed in a scene
Over matter-js when stable stacking, many bodies or a determinism claim from the engine author matter
Over rapier when only 2D is needed and a small C-style API is preferred
avoid_when: A few 2D bodies in the browser with no WASM wanted: matter-js
3D rigid bodies: rapier or jolt-physics-js
Scripted motion with no collisions: anime-js or theatre-js
notes: 2026-11-27: Bake, do not seek: step every frame from t=0 and cache positions. Vector getters return owned wasm objects; call .delete() on them. The compat and deluxe builds gave identical trajectories on one machine. The engine's cross-platform determinism claim is unverified here, and the binding's maintainer is a third party.

assessment.rationale: MIT for engine and binding; box2d3-wasm 6.0.0 (2026-10-26) installs with one pnpm dependency and runs in Node with no browser or system install. The lead named Homebrew stable 3.2.0; the npm binding pins a patched v3.2 fork. Adds an engine-author determinism claim that matter-js and pymunk do not make; the claim itself is not verified across platforms.

evidence.result: Three circles dropped on a floor, 90 steps at 1/30 s, 4 sub-steps in Node 22.19.0; trajectory JSON identical across two processes (SHA-256 d9b9285b...4b90) and across compat and deluxe builds; all finite, bounced, settled at y 0.4997, 0.4999, 0.7912; min y 0.3657.
evidence.scope: Rigid circles on a static box, one machine (macOS arm64); not joints, other shapes, other platforms, seeking, replay, or playback in a scene. Settling is incomplete at frame 89.

resources.name: occt-wasm
resources.role: OpenCascade CAD kernel in WebAssembly: exact solids, STEP/STL I/O and hidden-line SVG in Node
resources.summary: OpenCascade V8 compiled to WebAssembly with a typed TypeScript API. From one pnpm dependency, Node builds exact solids (primitives, booleans, fillets, sweeps), reads and writes STEP, STL and BREP, tessellates for three-js or babylon-js, and draws hidden-line views as SVG or PNG. It is the JavaScript route to exact CAD, with no Python.
use_when: Exact dimensioned parts and STEP I/O inside a Node or browser pipeline; over build123d when Python is unwanted
Tessellate a solid straight into a three-js or babylon-js scene
Hidden-line technical views as SVG for the svg and resvg chain
avoid_when: Python CAD scripts with a builder API: build123d
Viewing or converting CAD files with a GUI or CLI: mayo
Lighting, materials and final frames: blender-background or three-js
resources.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 for the wrapper and build tooling; the compiled WASM is LGPL-2.1-only (inherits OCCT), so the .wasm must stay replaceable
notes: 2026-11-27: Lead said 5.17.2; npm latest is 5.18.6 (modified 2026-11-25). Requires WASM SIMD, tail calls and wasm exceptions; no IGES. Node 22 lacks `using` syntax, so dispose the kernel by hand.

resources.name: OpenColorIO
resources.role: Colour-management engine for ACES and config-driven transforms; library plus ocio* CLI utilities
resources.summary: Academy Software Foundation colour-management library. A config file defines colour spaces, looks and views; applications use the C++ or Python API (or the ocioconvert and ociocheck utilities) to transform pixels between them. Used inside OpenImageIO, Blender, Natron and most VFX tools. Strength: authoritative, config-driven ACES and scene-referred transforms; it processes colour, not files.

Validating or authoring an OCIO config the whole pipeline will share
Over ad-hoc ImageMagick colourspace flags when transforms must match Blender or Natron
avoid_when: Reading, writing or resizing files: oiiotool or ImageMagick, which call OCIO
Simple sRGB to linear conversion: ImageMagick is enough
Browser display: use a canvas colour space, OCIO has no JS runtime here

resources.name: OpenImageIO / oiiotool

resources.summary: oiiotool is the command-line front end to OpenImageIO. It reads and writes EXR, TIFF, PNG, DPX, HDR and many more, keeps an image stack processed left to right, and offers resize, crop, composite, diff, metadata editing and --colorconvert via OpenColorIO. Sequences are addressed with frame wildcards, --frames and --parallel-frames. Strength: float, multichannel and colour-managed work that ImageMagick handles poorly.

resources.summary: TypeGPU (Software Mansion) wraps WebGPU with schemas that are at once GPU types, CPU buffer layouts and TypeScript types, and compiles 'use gpu' TypeScript functions to WGSL through the unplugin-typegpu build plugin. tgpu.resolve returns the generated WGSL as a string. Distinguishing strength: typed, composable shaders for plain WebGPU, with shader output that can be snapshotted.
use_when: Typed buffers, bind groups and pipelines over raw WebGPU calls, in a browser scene or in Node with dawn-node-webgpu
Shader logic written once in TypeScript and shared with CPU code, with the generated WGSL pinned by a snapshot
avoid_when: Shaders inside a Three.js scene: three-js-shading-language
WebGL targets: twgl or regl
A single hand-written WGSL pass where the raw API is shorter: webgpu

install.macos: pnpm add typegpu && pnpm add -D unplugin-typegpu

notes: 2026-11-27: lead said 0.12.10 and an unverified plugin name; npm latest is typegpu 0.12.12 and the plugin is unplugin-typegpu (latest 0.12.9, lagging the library). Node use with dawn-node-webgpu was unverified in the lead and is now shown by the example.

assessment.rationale: MIT, active (repo pushed 2026-11-19, npm 0.12.12). Nearest neighbours are raw webgpu, three-js-shading-language (Three.js only) and WebGL helpers; none gives typed WGSL authoring for plain WebGPU. Pre-1.0 API, and the build plugin lags the library; no system install needed.

evidence.result: 'use gpu' vertex and fragment functions plus a typed uniform struct resolved to WGSL (snapshotted), 3 frames 64x64 rgba8unorm via webgpu 0.6.2 Metal (apple metal-3); max channel deviation 0 vs analytic reference; shuffled equals sequential; two runs byte-identical; Node v22.19.0, unplugin-typegpu 0.12.9; contact sheet inspected.
evidence.scope: typegpu 0.12.12 with unplugin-typegpu 0.12.9 Node hook, one render pipeline and uniform, Node 22 on macOS arm64 Metal. Not browsers, compute, textures sampling, other backends or performance.

resources.name: Vizzu
resources.role: Animated charts that morph between chart types (bar, stacked, scatter) in a browser canvas, seekable
resources.summary: Vizzu (vizzu npm package, C++ compiled to WASM) draws charts to a canvas and animates between chart states with chart.animate(), keeping each data marker as one object through bar, stacked, scatter, pie and similar changes. A keyframe array is one paused AnimControl whose seek() takes a time, so the harness can drive it from t. Strength: object-constant data-story transitions without hand-built tweens.
use_when: A data story where one set of marks morphs between chart types; over d3, which leaves transitions to the author
Bar, stacked and scatter views of one table as a single seekable timeline
A chart scene that must be captured frame by frame through packages/capture
avoid_when: Bespoke marks or full geometry control: d3 with SVG
A static chart image with no motion: vl-convert
Alpha output: the fixture draws on an opaque background and alpha is untested
notes: 2026-11-27: determinism needed the scene's seek to call control.seek twice; with one call, shuffled capture differed from sequential in 3 of 5 runs (one random frame each). Untested whether a longer settle fixes it instead.

assessment.rationale: npm vizzu 0.18.0 and GitHub v0.18.0 both 2026-04-20; repository last pushed the same day (7 months ago), not archived; Apache-2.0; 2,051 stars. Object-constant chart-type morphs that d3 and vl-convert lack; seekable via AnimControl.

evidence.result: 90 1280x720 frames of a 3 s bar, stacked, scatter keyframe chain seeked via AnimControl; shuffled equals sequential in 16 of 16 runs with a double seek, 2 of 5 with a single seek (one random frame differed); 69 to 70 distinct frames; frame 90 differs. Frames inspected.
evidence.scope: Paused keyframe chain seek on macOS arm64, Chromium via Playwright, screenshot route. Needs a double seek; opaque background only, no alpha; end-of-chain seek checked once; no other charts or fonts.

resources.name: Web Audio API
resources.role: Browser audio graph; OfflineAudioContext renders deterministic audio faster than real time
resources.summary: Node-graph audio API for oscillators, buffers, filters, gain automation and analysis. A live AudioContext plays in real time; an OfflineAudioContext renders the graph to an AudioBuffer as fast as possible, which suits VCR. Encode the buffer to WAV and mux with ffmpeg. For audio-reactive visuals compute per-frame features from the decoded buffer: AnalyserNode is real-time, and under OfflineAudioContext needs suspend(t) per frame. No beat or onset detection.
use_when: Rendering generated sound effects or beds offline into a WAV, no dependencies
Audio analysis (FFT) feeding visuals, computed from a decoded buffer
Over Tone.js when you only need a few oscillators, filters or gain ramps
avoid_when: Musical scheduling, instruments and effects: Tone.js
Mixing and fading existing files: ffmpeg
Live playback during capture: not deterministic
notes: 2026-10-26: Autoplay policy and headless audio output not checked; OfflineAudioContext avoids both in principle.

assessment.rationale: AudioContext and OfflineAudioContext supported since Chrome 35 per MDN browser-compat-data; stable and standard-track.

evidence.result: OfflineAudioContext rendered 48,000 mono samples at 48 kHz; measured 440 Hz. Attack/sustain/release/tail RMS 0.173235/0.353553/0.183994/0.021141. Two buffers and WAVs matched; WAV SHA-256 e9971bd52252fc57655ddff3178222e040c75b6ca669ccaf56a31c84dda8e9a5; ffprobe: pcm_s16le, mono, 48 kHz, 1.000000 s. Not auditioned.
evidence.scope: Chrome 156 OfflineAudioContext, 48 kHz mono 440 Hz sine with gain envelope; repeat buffer/WAV checks. No live playback, other browsers or audio sources.

resources.name: WebCodecs
resources.role: Frame-exact browser video/audio encoders and decoders; pair with a muxer
resources.summary: Low-level API (VideoEncoder, VideoDecoder, AudioEncoder, ImageDecoder, VideoFrame) for encoding and decoding media without a container. Feed it VideoFrames made from a canvas with explicit timestamps and it returns encoded chunks; a muxer such as Mediabunny writes the file. Frame-exact, unlike MediaRecorder. Needs fully specified codec strings; H.264 availability varies by build.

Decoding source video frames to seek without ffmpeg
Over MediaRecorder when output must not depend on wall-clock time
avoid_when: Finished MP4 with audio mux and filters: ffmpeg

notes: 2026-10-26: Codec support in headless Chromium (H.264, AAC) not verified; check isConfigSupported at runtime. MDN page states dedicated-worker availability but not secure-context status.

assessment.rationale: Standard-track, not experimental; Chrome 94 shipped VideoEncoder, VideoDecoder, AudioEncoder and ImageDecoder per MDN browser-compat-data.

evidence.result: VP8 encoder/decoder supported. Two passes each round-tripped 3 32x32 frames at (timestamp,duration) (0,33333),(33333,33333),(66666,33333) us; decoded mean RGB exactly red/green/blue (max channel error 0, tolerance 20). Functional metrics matched on repeat.
evidence.scope: Native WebCodecs VP8 encode/decode of three 32x32 solid frames in Chrome 156; exact timestamps/durations, dimensions and color checked. No muxing or other codecs.

resources.summary: The browser's OpenGL ES binding, in WebGL 1 and 2, used directly or through Three.js, PixiJS, OGL, regl and twgl. Rendering is a function of uniforms such as time, so frames can be drawn in any order. Headless Chromium falls back to software GL when no GPU is present, which is slow but works. Read pixels or screenshot the canvas.

Under Three.js, PixiJS or OGL: the default backend that works everywhere
Over WebGPU when headless or broad Chromium support matters today
avoid_when: Heavy compute or modern GPU features: WebGPU, where supported
Plain 2D drawing: Canvas 2D
Raw API verbosity: use Three.js, OGL, regl or twgl instead
notes: 2026-10-26: Software GL fallback speed in headless Chromium comes from general knowledge; not measured.

assessment.rationale: WebGL 1 since Chrome 9, WebGL 2 since Chrome 56 per MDN browser-compat-data; standard-track, not experimental.

Chrome 113 shipped it on ChromeOS, macOS and Windows; 144 added Linux on Intel Gen12+. Headless capture needs a working adapter, so check navigator.gpu.requestAdapter() and keep a WebGL fallback.
use_when: GPU compute or heavy particle and simulation work beyond what WebGL handles
Three.js WebGPURenderer and node materials on a machine with a GPU
Modern shader pipelines written in WGSL
avoid_when: Anything that must render on any machine: WebGL
Headless or CI renders without an adapter: WebGL on software GL
Simple 2D: Canvas 2D
notes: 2026-10-26: Headless Chromium adapter availability and required flags were not tested.

assessment.rationale: Chrome 113 on ChromeOS, macOS, Windows; 144 adds Linux (Intel Gen12+); Firefox 141, Safari 26 per MDN browser-compat-data. Not Baseline, so fallbacks are required.

resources.name: WhisperX
resources.role: Word-timed speech recognition and diarization
notes: 2026-11-01: faster-whisper ASR with forced alignment for word timestamps and optional diarisation.
2026-11-01: CPU-only on Apple Silicon; ML output drifts across versions, so commit alignment JSON as fixtures.
2026-11-15: v3.8.7rc1 is newer but prerelease; card and last_release identify the latest stable release. Diarization requires separate gated model access; model terms are not the code licence.
2026-11-24: guide written at skills/whisperx/SKILL.md from examples/whisperx-word-timing evidence (tiny.en int8 CPU, generated 10-word sentence); diarization and other models untested.

evidence.result: 10 words from macOS say (Samantha): WER 0/10 in both runs; 10/10 matched and timed, start error mean 0.033 s, max 0.077 s vs energy onsets (bound 0.20 s); transcripts identical; timings identical to 1 ms across runs. faster-whisper 1.2.1, torch 2.8.0, CPU int8.
evidence.scope: tiny.en int8 CPU, generated 10-word sentence: word error and start bounds, identical text on rerun. Not diarization, other models, real speech. macOS arm64.

resources.summary: Python CLI and library for batched automatic speech recognition with word-level timestamps, forced alignment, VAD and optional speaker diarization. It uses faster-whisper/Whisper and wav2vec2 alignment models; model downloads, accelerator stack and gated pyannote access for diarization add setup constraints. Its distinguishing strength is combining transcription and word alignment in one local workflow.
use_when: Generate word-timed transcripts from audio with local model inference
Use when forced alignment and optional speaker diarization justify the larger model stack
avoid_when: Need lightweight transcription without word alignment: use whisper-cpp
Use Rhubarb Lip Sync when output should be mouth-shape cues rather than transcript words
resources.license: BSD-2-Clause (code); pretrained models and gated diarization models carry separate terms/access requirements

install.macos: uv tool install whisperx (follow upstream platform and PyTorch guidance; model downloads required)

assessment.rationale: WhisperX v3.8.6 released 2026-05-25 and the official repository shows active 2026 issues and pull requests; v3.8.7rc1 is a later prerelease. Code is BSD-2-Clause; pretrained and gated diarization models have separate terms/access.
